findings.proof: Tier 1's container: `sh scripts/test-mutate.sh check <change> <test file>` run several times for a sample of the flipped changes, Backend._install's first, until the test whose result varies is named; then that test run many times in a row on the unchanged code and on one change, with the same result each time.
findings.note: Not a finding of the review: an older hardening issue with no severity and no work-pad id. The fact to find first is which test's result varies, and why; the remedy and the files follow from it, so the one file listed is a guess (the file whose `be` fixture every backend test shares). A hint from the issue's own table: changes in _adopt_windows_setup, which returns at once on Linux, were 'killed' in one run, so some kills came from a test that fails by itself now and then (or a crash at exit, the table's 'other'), not from a test that reaches the change. `mutate.py check`'s verdict is #573's subject: it prints caught for any failing pytest status. #487's new tests run real worker threads, so they must wait for their workers, or they add to this.

findings.proof: A new case in tests/test_trust.py, beside test_gpg_trust_with_published_key: an OpenPGP Authority whose key has an expiry, a commit signed after that date (gpg's --faked-system-time, or a key made with a short expiry), and the extended key published in `.appkata/keys/`: the sync fetches the key again, stores it and applies the commit; a copy with another primary fingerprint is not taken; a revoked copy stops the next commit. findings.note: Decided 2026-11-24: At every sync, from the Trust's own repository only: each sync reads the keys the Trust publishes in `.appkata/keys/` and takes a newer copy of an Authority's key; the keyserver is asked only when a key has expired and the repository has no newer copy. The sort's note, written before the decision, for what it says of the parts and the files: It was read, never run (it needs a key past its expiry); the unit's proof covers that. One part is the owner's: when a key is fetched again apart from an expiry. The remedy says "and at some interval otherwise" and names none, and a timed fetch sends every OpenPGP Authority's fingerprint to keys.openpgp.org again and again, a contact that #262 asks whether to keep at all: the two are asked together, and #262's ruling comes first (if the lookup is limited to `.appkata/keys/`, the keyserver half of every option here goes). Ready as it stands: on a check that ends in an expired key, the key is looked up again the way `_lookup_gpg_key` does, a copy is taken only when its primary fingerprint is the Authority's, it is stored and the commit is checked once more. A new copy should be merged into the stored one (gpg --import), not replace it, so an older copy without a revocation can't undo one. devtools.gpg_keygen makes keys that never expire, so the test's key needs a parameter there or its own gpg call. The record is for the recommended option; the button changes src/appkata/backend.py and src/appkata/qml/TrustPanel.qml and R7.6.5 as well.
